## Purpose

Read the current communication ownership generation before a cutover CAS, and
inspect the first channel switch and compatibility deadline for each destination.

## Access and usage

Only the local operator or daemon can invoke this command. Worker, supervisor
and playbook identities cannot use it to acquire operator authority.

```bash
aq ask cutover-status --project-id PROJECT --json
```

Use the `generation` for `result.configured_destination` as the next
`aq ask cutover --expected-generation` value. Handle a stale CAS by inspecting
status again; another operator may have advanced the mode after this snapshot.

## Result and persistence

`result.destinations` lists the project's recorded destinations in destination
order, including the configured destination as legacy/generation 0 if absent.
Each entry reports mode, generation, migrated flag, first-switch UTC and both
Unix-second and UTC compatibility deadlines. UTC strings use ISO 8601; timestamps
are null until the first channel switch. The first switch is derived from the
immutable deadline minus 30 days and remains stable through rollback and re-enable.

The handler reads `human_communication_modes` through
`src/asks/transport_controls.py:cutover_status`. It creates no rows, advances no
generations, changes no deadlines and sends no external messages.

See the [status contract](../../specs/design/human-ask-cutover-status.md) and
[operator runbook](../../guides/human-asks-rollout.md).

## Failure modes

Missing or empty `project_id` returns `ask.invalid_input`. Agent HTTP requests
are refused by the operator scope check; direct non-operator calls are also
rejected by the handler. A database failure is not an empty status report.
